title: Stationary macroscopic Fourier orbit with leading negative defect

orbit_law.shell: Choose ell_N a power of two with N/16<=ell_N<=N/8, d_N=ell_N^3, and monomial-translate the K1646 cube into one fixed positive-frequency shell.
orbit_law.field: For independent uniform Y in T^3 and Theta in [0,2pi), M_N(x)=sqrt(2)A_N Re[e^(iTheta)R_N(x+Y)] with A_N^2=eta/N.
orbit_law.symmetries: Uniform Y makes the law stationary; Theta shifted by pi makes it centrally symmetric.
orbit_law.moments: At every x, v_(M,N)=A_N^2d_N and E M_N(x)^4=(3/2)A_N^4 int|R_N|^4.
orbit_law.coordinate_covariance: Each selected real sine and cosine coordinate has added variance delta s_k=omega_k A_N^2=eta omega_k/N.
orbit_law.scope_guard: The leading defect comes from one angularly coherent macroscopic block. It does not by itself control Fisher cost or prove energy descent.
